$description: SOLAR Divider: public API, platform states, slots and style recipe in token names. Generated by @bwp-web/codegen from docs/solar-web. Do not edit; decisions go in spec/overlay/, and the ones applied are listed under overlay.

gap.reason: Same value, governed token: a gap Figma leaves unbound at 0 is the none of its family, and SOLAR picks the family by direction, as its own bound gaps do: a horizontal auto layout's gap is an inset, a vertical one's a stack (the Foundations agent reference and the Spatial chapter). Decided once here, as the paddings are.

paddingTop.reason: Same value, governed token: a padding Figma leaves unbound at 0 is inset.none, SOLAR's token for no inset. It is the one answer in every component, so it is decided once here and raised with SOLAR once, as a whole, not per component.

docs.description: Visual separator between content sections. Horizontal (full-width, inset, or with centered label) and vertical orientations. Mirrors Tailwind UI divider patterns.

rules.reason: Bespoke on both platforms, not MUI's Divider or Flutter's: SOLAR's divider is a rule, a label between two rules, or an inset rule, as layers of their own. MUI draws its rule as a border and a labelled one as two pseudo-elements, and Flutter's Divider takes no label, so neither can be drawn, or measured, layer by layer.
A labelled divider centres its label between the rules; a plain rule starts it.
A vertical divider lays its rule out down, a horizontal one across.
The gap between the label and its rules; a plain rule has none.
As the width; a labelled divider is as tall as its label's row.
The inset type is the rule indented by inset.md; the others start at the edge.
Its extent is the orientation's: a horizontal divider spans its container, a vertical one is its rule's thickness.
As the width, turned for a vertical divider.
The rule fills the divider's length and is a hairline across it.
